title: Forgiver of sin, accepter of return
hook: the surah opens with names: forgiver of sin, accepter of repentance (40:3)

segments.voice: Yesterday, led in groups, and your line was greeted with peace. Did you greet someone first, and mean it? Today, a new surah, Ghafir, the Forgiver. Day five hundred sixty-one.

When you meet someone important, the introduction often tells you what to expect. Doctor so-and-so, head of surgery. Judge so-and-so. A title says how they'll treat you. Surah forty begins with an introduction like that. After two opening letters, Ha Mim, and a line saying the book comes from Allah, the Mighty, the Knowing, it lists four titles in a row. And the order, and the balance between them, says a great deal about who's being introduced. The first one gives the surah its name.

Verse three. Pickthall: "The Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, the Stern in punishment, the Bountiful." In Arabic: ghafiri'dh-dhanb, wa qabili't-tawb, shadidi'l-'iqab, dhi't-tawl. Count them. Two names about mercy. Then one about severity. Then one about generosity. By the time severity is named, mercy has been named twice, and generosity has the last word. Ghafir, forgiver, comes from a root that means to cover. A mighfar is a helmet, the thing that covers and protects the head. So forgiving, in this word, is covering a sin so that it doesn't harm you. Qabil at-tawb: the one who accepts the return. Tawb is turning back. And qabil is the one who accepts, who takes what is brought to him. Commentators note the two titles are close but not the same: one covers what was done, the other accepts the person who comes back. Then the verse ends: there is no god but Him, and to Him is the journey. Everyone is traveling the same way, toward Him. A few verses later comes an image that's easy to miss. Verse seven: the angels who carry the Throne, and those around it, glorify their Lord and ask forgiveness for the believers. They say: our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who turn back and follow Your way. So the surah opens by introducing a Forgiver, and then shows angels praying for those who return. The surah has two names: some call it Ghafir, the Forgiver, and some call it Al-Mu'min, the Believer, after tomorrow's story.
screen: `TWO NAMES OF MERCY, ONE OF SEVERITY.`

segments.voice: The practice: repent of one thing. Sit, and let your breath settle. Choose one specific thing, not your whole life, one thing, that you'd like to turn back from. Name it to yourself honestly. If you pray, you can say astaghfirullah, I ask Allah's forgiveness, and picture the turning being accepted. If not, simply decide one way to set it right. Then sit in the quiet after the turning. The bell holds the time.
Forgiver of sin. Ghafir adh-dhanb, the first title in Surah Ghafir: the One who covers sin, beside the Accepter of return. Today's word.
Your line: he accepts the return. Today, when someone comes back to you after a mistake, accept it warmly, without making them earn it twice. Day five hundred sixty-one.

howItsDone: Muslims call on Allah as al-Ghafur and at-Tawwab in their prayers, and many say astaghfirullah repeatedly each day, following the Prophet's practice of seeking forgiveness often.

match.prompt: the four titles in 40:3 — tap the pairs.

myth: Surah Ghafir opens with severity before mercy
two names of mercy come first, then one of severity, then generosity.
the root of ghafir is linked to covering, as in a helmet
a mighfar is a helmet: forgiving covers and protects.
in the same surah, angels ask forgiveness for those who turn back
verse seven: the Throne-bearers pray for them.

fork.setup: Surah Ghafir introduces Allah with four titles. which comes first?
fork.reveal: the Forgiver of sin, then the Accepter of return, and only then severe in punishment, with the Bountiful last.

original.note: Arabic: the Forgiver of sin and the Accepter of return (40:3).

trapdoor: what you thought: God forgives, and also punishes.
what it means: the surah introduces Allah with two names of mercy, one of severity and one of bounty, in that order.
what a scholar hears: gh-f-r carries covering (mighfar, helmet); qabil is the verb for receiving; 40:7 has the Throne-bearers asking forgiveness for the penitent; the surah is also called Al-Mu'min.

sources.quoted: The Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, the Stern in punishment, the Bountiful.
